audit_metadata.methodology: npm audit + lock file analysis + supply chain inspection

grade_rationale: 5 critical CVEs + 15 high + vitest 3 versions behind = exceeds B-grade threshold (max P1=0, P2≤8)

critical_vulnerabilities.title: JavaScript Injection via AST Type Confusion
critical_vulnerabilities.description: Attackers can inject arbitrary JavaScript by tampering with @partial-block partial

critical_vulnerabilities.title: IPv4-mapped IPv6 Trust Subnet Spoofing
critical_vulnerabilities.description: Callers can spoof IP addresses via IPv4-mapped IPv6 format (::ffff:192.0.2.1) to bypass IP-based access control

critical_vulnerabilities.title: Prototype Pollution → RCE via Worker Options
critical_vulnerabilities.description: Prototype pollution in worker pool options allows arbitrary code execution during test execution
critical_vulnerabilities.fix: Upgrade vitest to v5.1.0+ (requires npm install vitest@^5.1.0)

critical_vulnerabilities.title: Code Injection via bytes Field Defaults
critical_vulnerabilities.description: Malformed protobuf messages can inject code into generated toObject() method

critical_vulnerabilities.title: Second prototype pollution gadget
critical_vulnerabilities.description: Related to tinypool in Frontend test harness

source_frontend.blocker: vitest@2.0.5 is 3+ versions behind, pins multiple critical vulnerabilities
source_frontend.action: URGENT: npm install vitest@^5.1.0, then npm update remaining packages

source_e2e.note: Playwright-based test ecosystem has excellent security profile

platform_orchestrator.supply_chain_note: 150 transitive dependencies warrant monthly auditing and SRI/integrity verification for critical gRPC deps

dependency_tree_size.risk_assessment: Medium — good for team project, monitor transitive changes

license_compliance.details: All packages MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD, no GPL/AGPL viral risk, no UNLICENSED

supply_chain.duplicate_versions: Expected (dev vs prod), no blockers identified

immediate.command: cd Source/Backend && npm update proxy-addr && cd ../../platform/orchestrator && npm update proxy-addr
immediate.reason: Critical IP spoofing vulnerability with high exploitability
Blocks 2 critical vulnerabilities (tinypool, mocker), 3 major versions behind

high: Full npm audit --depth=20 after immediate updates
policy: Enforce monthly npm audits on all packages (not just production)
Add vitest to watch list (track major version lag)
Add proxy-addr to watch list (recurring risk)
Document dependency update SLA in CLAUDE.md (critical: 7 days, high: 30 days)
Consider npm-check-updates (npm-check-updates -u --doctorTest) for safe bulk updates

post_fix: npm audit --json re-run on all packages (expect 0 critical + high)
git diff --stat (review scope of dependency updates)

learnings.vitest_risk: Vitest accumulates vulnerabilities when >2 major versions behind. Recommend quarterly update cycles with full test coverage.
learnings.build_tools_underappreciated: Dev dependency vulnerabilities are as critical as production. npm audit --depth=20 on all workspace packages.
learnings.proxy_addr_recurring: Watch list item. Update path: express@latest pulls proxy-addr@latest.
learnings.good_supply_chain_hygiene: No post-install scripts detected. Continue enforcement in onboarding.
learnings.e2e_clean: Playwright test ecosystem is clean. Consider as model for new test frameworks.
